page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix operations, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0, placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance, reaching 34.85 GB/sec and 15.13 GB/sec respectively. However, multi-core and memory performance are more constrained. The stress-ng multi-core CPU metric falls into the bottom 25% at 4403.68, and the Passmark memory score of 1586.87 is weak, reflecting uncached read memory bandwidth of 32.55 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 20.39 GB/sec.

Given its high compute-to-memory ratio and strong single-core capabilities, the c4n-highcpu-4 is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving averaging 8.93 GB/sec static throughput, Redis operations at 6.0 million SET operations per second, and small-scale LLM prompt processing. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, large-scale multi-threaded compilation, or heavy multi-core parallel processing due to its memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling limitations.
